title: Narrowest covering range
prompt:
Several sensors each logged the timestamps of their alerts as a sorted list. Find the shortest time window [a, b] that contains at least one timestamp from every sensor. Return it as [a, b]. If several windows are equally short, return the one with the smallest a.

- lists has 1 to 100 lists, each sorted ascending with 1 to 500 integers.
- Timestamps are between -10^5 and 10^5.
- The window length is b − a, and a window may have a == b.
hints: Take the first value of every list. The window from their minimum to their maximum covers every sensor.
To find a shorter window, the only useful move is to drop the current minimum and replace it with the next value from the same list.
A min-heap gives the current minimum; track the maximum as you push. Stop when the list of the popped minimum runs out.

solution.py:
import heapq

def narrowest_range(lists):
    heap = [(lst[0], i, 0) for i, lst in enumerate(lists)]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    high = max(lst[0] for lst in lists)
    best = [heap[0][0], high]
    while True:
        low, i, j = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if high - low < best[1] - best[0]:
            best = [low, high]
        if j + 1 == len(lists[i]):
            return best
        nxt = lists[i][j + 1]
        high = max(high, nxt)
        heapq.heappush(heap, (nxt, i, j + 1))
solution.explanation: Keep exactly one value from each list in a min-heap, plus the largest of them. The heap top and that maximum form a window covering every list. Pop the minimum, record the window if it is shorter, then push the next value from that list and update the maximum. Moving any other pointer could only widen the window, so this sweep checks every window that could be best. Once a list is exhausted no covering window can start later. Strict < keeps the earliest window on ties because a only grows.

complexity.notes: n is the total number of timestamps and k the number of lists. Each value is pushed and popped once, and the heap never holds more than k entries.

followUps: Return the window as indexes into each list as well.
The lists are streams that never end. Report the best window seen after each alert.
